discovery: Microscopic origin of black hole entropy and the holographic gauge/gravity duality

nominees.name: Juan Maldacena
nominees.affiliation: Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, USA

motivation: In 1996 Strominger and Vafa counted the bound states of D-branes and exactly reproduced the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of a black hole, A/4G, from microscopic quantum states. This was the first statistical-mechanical derivation of black hole entropy, a problem open since Bekenstein and Hawking. Building on these brane constructions, Maldacena proposed in 1997 that quantum gravity in anti-de Sitter space is exactly equivalent to a non-gravitational gauge theory on its boundary. This holographic duality made unitarity of black hole evaporation concrete and became a basic tool across physics, from strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma to quantum information and condensed matter. Its quantitative predictions have been checked by exact methods: superconformal indices, localization and integrability now reproduce the entropy of AdS black holes from field theory. Together these works turned black hole thermodynamics into a precise statement about quantum states, transforming our understanding of quantum gravity.
